assertions.name: log_normaliser_A_exponent
assertions.source: log-log slope of log Z(3A) over A=2..64 vs the SEMF volume-term exponent

description: ROAST-M2 exponent-only test of the A-nucleons -> 3A-strands map: does the framework reproduce the extensive (A^1) exponent with magnitude free?

discriminating_power.note: Measured 1.674 on A=2..64 and rising to 1.995 on A=1024..4096 -- asymptotically 2, approached slowly because of the linear term. Either way it is NOT 1, so the exponent test does discriminate between the corpus's actual normaliser and a plausible alternative, and would also detect an affine strand rule n = 3A + c, c != 0. The test is therefore not vacuous.

SCALE_CORRECTION_2026_08_31.what_is_wrong: Every MeV figure in this witness uses m_e = 0.511 MeV as the energy scale, with no justification given. The corpus's binding machinery uses E_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) = 4.18598 MeV.
SCALE_CORRECTION_2026_08_31.what_is_UNAFFECTED: The exponent test itself. A constant multiplier cannot change a log-log slope, so log_normaliser_A_exponent = 1 and the (1+q^2)^n closed form stand, and so does the verdict that the braid->nucleus map is not the defective step.

data.verdict: EXPONENT TEST PASSES (unaffected by the scale correction above; a log-log slope is scale-free). The 3-strands-per-nucleon map yields a normaliser whose logarithm is exactly linear in A -- the SEMF volume term's exponent -- with the coefficient constant to all computed digits. This is a NEGATIVE for the ROAST's R2 hypothesis that the braid->nucleus map is the defective step: the map's A-scaling is right. The residual is a pure multiplicative constant, not a shape error. Deliberately not matched to any structural candidate (see module docstring).
